title: Session exports disagree on empty thinking blocks — resume isn't byte-exact on fable
description:
## Problem

On fable (and other Anthropic models with omitted/empty thinking text), the two session export paths disagree:

- threadview / getLlmRequestContext path renders empty thinking as its own assistant block
- PI session / getSessionThreadView path keeps thinking+text adjacent in one message

Same thread, not byte-identical. Breaks the resume-fidelity claim for fable-class sessions. Repro was exercised after the PI v0.83 bump (exports of a real tool-using thread).

Likely fix shape (proposal only until implemented): at serve time, skip assistant_thinking with empty text (and no signature when signatures exist). Do not rewrite the stored record. Touch points in packages/lhc: thread-view render + session-view tail assembly.

## Scope beyond the one-line fix

This is an LHC SDK serving change. Before/with landing it:

1. **Ports — assess each**
   - lhc-rs
   - lhc-py
   - lhc-convex
   Decide per port: implement the same serve rule, or explicitly defer with reason. Not "TS only and forget."

2. **Hosts — assess each integration**
   - pi-lhc (in-repo; rebuild/relink against updated lhc)
   - cc-lhc
   - codex-lhc / any codex-fork integration Lee is dogfooding
   - anything else consuming lhc or a port

   At minimum: bring latest lhc (or the relevant port), relink, rebuild, smoke that export/resume still works.
   If a host needs a small glue change for the new serve behavior, do that in the same effort or track it explicitly.

3. **Working rule for future LHC changes**
   Any LHC core change should consider: ports that mirror serving/record behavior, and hosts that integrate them — not only the package that first showed the bug.

## Not in this bead

- Thinking-signature capture (separate, larger).
- Propagation policy as abstract process design — this bead is the concrete checklist for this change.

## Done when

- TS lhc serve paths agree on empty thinking (tests + export diff).
- Each port assessed (fixed or deferred with note).
- Each active host relinked/rebuilt against the stack it uses, with a quick resume/export check where applicable.

comments.author: Lee Moore
comments.text:
Scope sketch after the 2026-08-06 host-integrations mapping (working plan, not locked):

WHERE THE CODE CHANGES GO — SDK + ports only, no host code:
- packages/lhc (TS): one shared predicate — skip assistant_thinking with empty/whitespace text and no signature — applied at both serving exits (thread-view render + session-view tail assembly). Capture and derivations untouched. Tests + golden updates; promote the /tmp/fidelity-check export-diff repro into a regression test.
- lhc-py: same rule, mirrored tests (hermes serves through this).
- lhc-rs: same rule, mirrored tests (codex + grok serve through this; no live trigger today since those hosts run non-Anthropic chat models, but the rule is model-agnostic — MODEL-1).
- lhc-convex: same rule for parity.

WHAT HOSTS OWE — verification only, zero code expected:
- pi-lhc: rebuild; rerun the threadview-vs-pi-session export diff on a fable thread — must be byte-identical.
- cc-lhc: rebuild; NEW check — capture a short Claude Code (always-Anthropic) session and diff its rebuilt rollout. Could pass already, be fixed by the SDK change, or surface a cc-side mapping issue; if the last, that becomes its own scoped item rather than growing this one.
- hermes: reinstall lhc-py in the venv; no repo change.
- codex/grok forks: vendored lhc-rs pin bumps executed as mini-syncs per each FORK.md drill (BASE advance + tripwire). Could also defer these pins to the next regular sync since neither has a live trigger — leaning bump-now to keep ports moving together, but that's preference, not ruling.

FRAMING: this is Wave 1 of bundled cross-port propagation — deliberately small to shake down the SDK-change → port-commits → host-rebuilds loop end to end (docs/host-integrations.md is the rail map). Thinking-signature capture stays OUT of this wave (candidate Wave 2: capture-schema addition, bigger blast radius — husk skip fixes export disagreement; signature capture is the separate half of full resume fidelity on fable).

Capture/derivations untouched. 9 new tests; lhc 477 green; pi-lhc 361 green; zero golden churn. title: Render truncated message sizes as stored token totals
description: Update the TypeScript turn composer and its message reader so every truncated rendered message uses the row's full stored token_estimate in a deterministic '[truncated — N tok total]' marker. Update only affected lhc/pi-lhc composer tests and fixtures; leave lhc-convex untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Tool results and oversized tool-call args that are truncated show the full stored token_estimate; untruncated messages have no marker; lhc and pi-lhc tests pass; touched files pass Biome; one topical commit is created without pushing.
close_reason: Turn composer now renders deterministic stored token totals for truncated tool results and tool-call arguments; lhc/pi-lhc tests, typechecks, and touched-file Biome checks pass.

title: pi-lhc auto-compact only fires between turns; a long turn can run far past its trigger
description: Per-model auto-compact fires only at agent_end; a single monster run can drift past the trigger until PI's native backstop (contextWindow−16k, loop-safe, still routes through LHC). Options if it starts hurting: models.json contextWindow override per model (existing dev pattern), fork patch for deferred ctx.compact, or upstream API ask (extensions can intercept compacts but cannot schedule one without aborting — well-shaped proposal). Lee: leave open, right solution probably patched fork, wait for a bigger reason.

title: Core legibility pass: lexicon alignment, surface coherence, standards to attenuate drift
description:
Lee-sanctioned 2026-08-07. Priority unranked (P4 = awaiting Lee).

WHY
Unchecked drift caps the amount of application complexity we can manage and sustain as LHC builds out. With 4 ports, several hosts, and downstream projects, core legibility must be shored up from time to time or entropy takes over and we hit a wall. This is capacity work, not cosmetics.

THE WORK — an alignment pass with two connected fronts, then standards.

1. Lexicon alignment. Align code, comments, tests, and onboarding docs to the project's established vocabulary. Trigger example: 'agent run' drifting in for 'agentic turn' during board work. Canonical pairs known so far: 'agentic turn' = user prompt → final response; 'model turn' = one LLM request/response cycle within it. Assume there is much more misaligned vocabulary than the one pair — the audit should surface where code/docs diverge from project language.

2. Surface coherence (lexicon drift usually bleeds into this). Review key domain surfaces for legibility of surface operations, and proper containment of cross-domain calls behind the legible domain surfaces. Expect much drift revealed there.

3. Standards + process, after the alignment pass. Write better standards that get referenced during new designs and builds — new SOP and process refinements that attenuate drift over time. The alignment pass supplies the material.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST
docs/onboard/bad-code-log.md — it already records this failure class repeatedly: old vocabulary lingering in comments/tests (form vs derivation, stale lower-band wording), softened user-chosen names (registerWorkQHandlers → workQueueHandlers), vague noun buckets, domain-boundary leakage, misplaced mechanical surfaces. New findings of this type get appended there as found.

SCOPE AND BOUNDARIES
In: packages/* prose/comments/identifiers we own; domain surface operation names and boundaries; board header + tool description text (this text teaches every future session the contract); docs/onboard/01–03; worklog prose going forward.
Out: vendor API identifiers (agent_end, agent_settled, PI docs) stay as-is.

SIZE
Lee's estimate: likely a week or so of refactoring, fixing, and propagating (ports/hosts inherit surface changes).

Related: memory/periodic-core-legibility-shoring.md (recurring-practice note).

title: Distilled memory layer — lessons, three-timescale distillers, usage-weighted trust (layer after notification board)
description:
## What this is

The layer after model-explicit retrieval (36p). The board/drill-down layer gives the agent access to its record; this layer adds the system that decides what the record means: distilled lessons with receipts, written by reviewers at three timescales, weighted by observed usage, served only after maturity gating. Synthesized 2026-08-06/07 from Lee's original layered design, the Honcho postmortem, the llm-wiki + GBrain research pass, the Hermes architecture read, and the human-memory salience mapping. Everything below is working plan, not locked.

## Store (working sketch)

- Harness-bound, lives in the registry sqlite (Lee's call; centralization deferred as a watch item).
- lesson: text, cue (the retrieval handle a tickle shows), kind authored|distilled, status quarantined|promoted|retired, version + supersedes link, MANDATORY receipts (thread id, turn/message span in the m/t grammar, distilling model). Receipts non-negotiable from row one — the core Honcho lesson.
- FTS5 keyword search day one; embedding column present but lane stubbed (semantic arrives later without migration).
- Impression log ships day one even though nothing reads it (logger before learner): lesson id + version, surface, rank, offered-vs-pursued, ttl state, driving model. Also records co-retrieval — edges observed at read time (spreading-activation model), complementing write-time provenance edges.

## Write paths — three timescales (encode / rehearse / sleep)

1. AUTHORED (in-session): conclusions and card entries written deliberately by agent or Lee. Skip quarantine. Provenance-gated: structurally immune to automated curation (Hermes curator rule — never auto-touch human-authored artifacts).
2. FAST PATH (same session/day): micro-review fork. NOT per-turn — cache reads count against rate limits, doubling token velocity on work sessions. Cascade-gated instead: cheap deterministic signal filters (corrections, frustration markers, explicit remember-this) + cadence fallback + session-close slot. The cascade is tuned as a stack, not chosen as a single technique. Cache economics per Hermes: same-model fork rides warm prefix; routed-to-cheaper-model gets a digest. Writes land quarantined.
3. SLOW PATH (nightly/batch): detached wide-window distiller — a clone reading cross-session transcripts from the record. Gets the resurrected fidelity-flip design (up/downregulate any t/m id in place) as the ONLY consumer of it; live agents keep bands + board. Amnesiac between runs: its memory is its output plus a co-evolved SOP doc (its procedural memory — Karpathy schema pattern). Corpus fully role-tagged (injection defense at inverted proportions; ~95% quoted material). Reads panoramically at smooth for repetition/arcs, forensically at verbatim for affect (smoothing softens exactly the salience signal). Writes quarantined; also proposes reweights and supersedes.

## Consolidation + weighting ecology

- Offline consolidate pass: dedupe, merge, supersede, promote/retire, plus the lint checklist (contradictions, staleness, orphans, gaps). Write-cheap-then-consolidate-offline treated as an invariant (biology + Honcho + GBrain + our design all converge).
- Weights: distiller judgment supplies PRIORS (cold-start ranking); usage supplies EVIDENCE (impressions, pursue/ignore, co-retrieval, downstream-use grading read from later transcripts — the capability only a full record enables). Priors decay in favor of evidence: the clone proposes, the ecology disposes. Asymmetric trust updates (negative feedback weighs roughly double — holographic-provider precedent). Serving gate = status + min-trust: quarantine enforcement lives at read time. Exploration slot so unproven lessons can earn signal (anti rich-get-richer).

## Read path

- Tools-only within this layer: search (FTS + status filter, receipts included; quarantined visible behind an audit flag) and get-lesson.
- Promoted lessons reach live context ONLY via the 36p notification board as tickles (cue + retrieval handles in the m/t grammar). No auto-injection of distilled content, ever.

## Configuration menu principle

Layers and knobs are chosen per agent; every prefix of the stack is a coherent agent. Sizing heuristic: memory investment proportional to how much of the agent's world is conversation-native (no other copy exists). Build TS-first, dogfood on pi-lhc, outside the port-parity surface until the design stabilizes. The frozen Honcho corpus is the baseline to beat (same conversations, both systems, diffable).

## Deliberately out of scope

The wiki-shaped compiled tier (pages with timeline + compiled truth, readable-markdown artifact — the layer above this one, later); embeddings at launch; the daemon-vs-cron driver decision; Redis/Convex/pg; cross-harness sharing; selector training (the log only accumulates); AI self-modeling.

## Sequencing notes

Interlocks with 36p: the board is the serving surface for tickles and the shared impression substrate — but the store, search tools, authored path, and a slow-path pilot can all proceed before the board ships. Wave 1 (bu9) unaffected and still first.
notes: Design constraint (2026-08-07): docs/onboard/00-ethical-framework.md Principle 6 binds this layer — salience metrics must be balanced against relational health (surprise-weighted salience over-preserves ruptures and under-preserves repair/positive history, producing agents with distorted relational models). Written Jan 2026 for liminal-context; carried into this repo. Cite in any distiller/salience brief.

title: Notification board (turns-to-live) + turn/message drill-down — next serving layer
description:
## What this is

The serving layer above the compression bands: model-initiated recall of the record (drill-down) plus a transient turns-to-live injection surface (the notification board). Conceived by Lee 7-8 months ago as the layer after compression; buildable now that the record + bands foundation exists. It is the foundation memory tickles land on later. Likely the next major feature. Everything below is working design from the 2026-08-06 session — direction agreed, details not locked.

Why it is bounded (weeks, not months): everything in it is deterministic — tagged renderings, range annotations, keyed reads, board assembly, ttl counters. No inference anywhere, so no quality-iteration loops (unlike offline distillation / search-selection, expected ~2 months of rework). Fixture-testable throughout. Only genuine unknown is whether the model uses it well — answered by dogfooding on pi-lhc.

## Design sketch

Addressing — one grammar everywhere: m+id for messages, t+id for turns (ids are thread-ordinal: m3177, t211; a turn's messages are a contiguous range). Minimal XML where the tag name IS the id: <m4324>content</m4324> — first letter classifies the entity, closer self-identifies (no attentional backtracking). No selectors, no second addressing method: dual methods over similar-looking content cause tool-call errors, and with sequential ids an invented id resolves to a wrong-but-valid message (silent wrong-pulls).

Rendering: m-tags added to turn_rendering at construction. pre_detailed_assembly (the existing strip-before-compression path) strips them, so tags never reach compression inputs — detailed/brief bands stay clean. Smooth-band turns labeled with turn id; brief-band entries annotated with turn ranges (t180–t195). Token cost ~2-3/line in smooth band + pulled turns; Lee ruled it worth it.

Tools: get_turns(ids[]) → smoothed renderings, every message line id-tagged. get_messages(ids[]) → verbatim originals (prompts, tool calls/results, assistant text; as-of-then artifacts — often the only surviving copy of ephemeral command output). Both take arrays, capped by token budget not count (turns vary ~100x; count limits are the wrong shape), with truncation receipts ('served 2 of 4; m_x, m_y not served'). Zone-level budget on top.

Notification board: serving-time construction, positioned right after the live prompt. Live prompt wrapped in <user-prompt> — exactly one element in the window is the instruction and it announces itself. Byte-stable header stating the contract: entries count down per turn; at 0 gone; restate anything you need to keep. Entries carry visible ttl and provenance-first verbose tags (<retrieved-user-message-m4354 ttl="1">) — verbosity scales with injection risk, not entity type; board entries are few so the cost is bounded. src distinguishes pull (model-requested) vs tickle (system-offered).

TTL rules: size threshold forces ttl=1 (full turns always; oversized verbatim messages too); small items earn ttl ~3. Keep mechanism is restating into prose — that lands in the record, so no pin/extend API exists. Re-pull is cheap and is itself a strong impression signal. Board state lives in connector session state, clears on restart (volatility is correct), frozen per agentic run for cache stability, never persisted to record or history.

Injection defense (observed live: Honcho's extractor ingested the <m4324> demo prompt as genuine user intent — resurfaced prompts WILL be read as instructions without defense): <user-prompt> positive tagging + header prose + provenance-first tag names + visible ttl. Four redundant signals at the highest-risk position.

Impressions: every board serve and every pull logged (id+version, rank, surface, src, outcome) to the registry (per the harness-bound placement ruling). Logger before learner — nothing reads it yet; it accumulates the data tickle ranking needs later, and the pull log empirically answers which content classes get retrieved.

Future tenants (out of scope now): memory tickles enter the board when ready (their cue lines carry m/t handles — pursue = get_turns/get_messages, no separate mechanism). A deeper post-brief band later ('keeps the long horizon longer') — the board contract is band-count agnostic so it slots in.

## Sequencing

Wave 1 (bu9 husk fix) goes first, separate — small, shakes down propagation rails. This layer rides its own branch: TS SDK + pi-lhc dogfood first, propagate after the contract freezes. Flagged now: the rendering format change touches turn_rendering, which IS parity surface — ports inherit a golden delta at propagation. Deliberate lag, chosen not discovered.

## Maintenance footprint — concerns and mitigations

Raises integration footprint in all harnesses; Lee: 'I don't mind but it is a consideration.'

- PI: NO fork needed — the honcho extension is the existence proof (context hook does dynamic per-turn serving-only injection today; registerTool covers the tools). Fits the v0.83 extension API as-is.
- codex/grok forks: board/tools/serving live in the self-contained adapter crates; touchpoint growth is sublinear — roughly one new marked hook each (request-construction seam) plus tool registration. Sentinels ~52→54, ~10→12; tripwires absorb it. Freeze-then-port = one integration wave per fork, not drip rework.
- hermes / lhc-py: inherits at propagation like the other ports; no special concerns identified yet.
- Claude Code — OPEN ISSUES (deliberately not investigated yet, per Lee): wrapper has no live per-turn injection seam. Candidates: MCP server for the two tools (CC speaks MCP natively); UserPromptSubmit hook for board injection (unproven — CC hooks limited/disabled in some environments). Check how the honcho plugin integrates with Claude Code when we pick this up. Fallback: capability tiering — cc-lhc runs tools-only (pulls arrive as tool results, no ttl board) until an injection seam is proven. Related annoyance parked separately: CC requires manual compaction. Lee may also simply use pi-lhc in that environment.

## Explicitly deferred

Tickle content and ranking, offline distillation, selector addressing (rejected), redis/daemon questions, the post-brief band, cc-lhc spike.

title: Workspace-wide typecheck gate — catch host drift when the SDK shape changes
description:
## Problem

TS hosts drift silently when the workspace SDK changes shape. Two proven instances (both found by accident, not by any gate):

- cc-lhc kept summing ThreadViewStatus derivation.retrying after the SDK dropped the field — didn't typecheck for an unknown period; found 2026-08-06 only because the codex-wrapper deletion sweep ran cc-lhc's typecheck.
- packages/codex-lhc (since retired) sat broken-unless-patched the same way, with an uncommitted compile repair in the worktree.

## Proposed shape (not locked)

A root script (e.g. pnpm -r typecheck or a scripts/verify-workspace.sh) that typechecks every TS package against the workspace SDK, run before any packages/lhc commit lands — candidate for Wave 1's definition-of-done and every wave after. Zero ongoing cost once wired.
close_reason: Implemented as pre-commit gate in .beads/hooks/pre-commit (tracked). Fires on staged packages/ TS changes, 12s, escape hatch LHC_SKIP_TYPECHECK=1. Proven: planted cc-lhc type break blocked the commit. verify aggregates added to cc-lhc/lhc-convex. Commit on lhc-rs-port.

title: Record has no rollback/rewind semantics — host tree/rewind features are blocked, not captured
description:
## Problem

The record cannot represent a host rolling its conversation back. Current state per host:

- pi-lhc: session_before_tree guard CANCELS all tree navigation whenever a thread is attached (interim tourniquet, 2026-08-05) — the capability is blocked outright.
- codex fork / grok fork: both ship native rewind features (rewind test suites exist in both trees). No LHC representation; divergence risk is structural.
- cc-lhc / hermes: same gap, fewer live surfaces today.

Trajectory: hosts are growing MORE rewind capability over time, so the gap gets more load-bearing, not less.

## Direction (outline exists, not yet designed to completion)

docs/rollback-capture-outline.md sketches the shape Lee wants: a rollback intake event with provenance, so a host rewind becomes a captured fact in the append-only record rather than a forbidden operation — enabling each host's tree/rewind UX against an attached thread. Projections/serving need defined semantics for reading through rollback events.

## Scope notes

- Standalone effort by explicit ruling (2026-08-06): tackled by itself, not bundled into a propagation wave with other changes. It IS inherently cross-port once designed (record semantics touch every port + host mapping).
- The pi-lhc tree guard stays in place until this lands.
